rows: Several large trees were blown down over the eastern part of the county.
A small metal building was blown over at a fire station about 9 miles southeast of Emory, and trees and power lines were blown down across the southern portion of the county.
Roof damage occurred at several buildings including an apartment complex and a restaurant. Damage to trees was also reported.
Tree limbs down south of Emory.
Trees and power lines were blown down across the county. Storage buildings were thrown across the road near Alba, and portable buildings were tossed around along Highway 69 in Emory.
A large tree was knocked down on CR 4250 northwest of Emory.
The Sheriff's Office reported several trees were down across the county. Some trees were blocking roads and at least one tree fell on a house.
Quarter size hail fell in the city of Emory.
Several trees were reported down on several county roads near Emory.
Quarter size hail was reported 5 miles northeast of the intersection of US 69 and HWY 19.
Numerous trees were knocked down on the west side of Lake Fork, and also on Hwy 19, CR 3150, CR 3325, and CR 4400.
Numerous trees were blown down throughout the western half of the county.
A report was received via social media of trees down just east of Emory, TX.
Trained spotters observed and photographed a brief tornado near the south shore of Lake Fork.
Fire and rescue reported quarter sized hail near Highway 19 North and CR 3417.
A trained spotter reported dime to quarter sized hail in the town of Point, TX.
Emergency management reported golf-ball sized hail near the Lake Tawakoni Dam near the county line.
A public report indicated hen-egg sized hail south-southwest of the city of Emory, TX.
A trained spotter reported dime to quarter sized hail in Emory, TX.
Emergency management reported golf-ball to baseball sized hail along FM 779 near the county line.
Rains County Sheriff's Department reported a large tree down in the city of Emory, TX.

A report of ping ping pong ball sized hail was reported in Emory.
Rains County Sheriff's Department reported trees blocking County Road 1520 just west of the city of Point, TX.
Emergency management reported nickel size hail in the city of Emory, TX.
DPS reported quarter size hail approximately 4.5 miles west-northwest of the city of Emory, TX, near the intersection of U.S. Highway 69 and RCR 1310.
Emergency management reported multiple trees down in the cities of Point and Emory along Highway 69.
Emergency management reported a tree blown onto a home in the city of Point, TX.
Fire and rescue reported quarter-sized hail on FM Highway 47 near FM Highway 276, west of the city of Emory, TX.
A trained spotter reported half-dollar sized hail along County Road 1495 approximately 6 miles south-southwest of the city of Emory, TX.
Emergency management reported quarter-sized hail near the intersection of Highway 19 and County Road 1280 south of the city of Emory, TX.
Numerous trees down and several county roads blocked around Emory.
Straight-line winds damaged large trees and tree limbs, and caused minor damage to homes along a path near CR 2460 and 2440 to just northwest of Alba.
A few roof wall panels were blown off the Rains High School gymnasium.
A trained spotter reported baseball sized hail in Point, TX.

Trees and tree limbs were down on FM 514 and needed to be cleared off the roadway.

Emory Fire Station reported flagpoles bowing over in thunderstorm winds, small limbs blowing across parking lot, and the bay doors of the fire station bowing in. An mPing report also reported more notable tree damage in Emory.
Power lines were knocked down and major tree damage was reported on the NW side of Emory, TX on HWY 69.
Damage to trees, carports, and awnings was reported across Rains County.
